messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for model variant 'redwood-hotstart-v2' in canary pool. Current p99=2.6s (SLO 0.9s). Streaming stalls + elevated tail. Paging oncall: @maria-ong, @ashwin

maria-ong: I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking canary traffic proportions.

ashwin: seeing the same in tracing — long waits in model startup/compile step, not token generation. Possibly hotstart compilation thrash.

kevin: can you confirm whether this is correlated with the rollout window? I see a traffic ramp at 11:02 UTC.

maria-ong: yes, deploy-bot shows model rollout: redwood-hotstart-v2 -> 40% canary started at 11:02:14. full rollouts delayed.

deploy-bot: deploy-log: 
```
[11:02:14] rollout started: redwood-hotstart-v2
[11:02:40] target canary 40% traffic
[11:03:05] autoscaler triggered additional kernels
```

samira: hypothesis: the new variant triggers JIT/kernels on first use causing GPU scheduling spikes and KV cache thrash for small sessions. Streaming sessions get stalled until kernels finish.

ashwin: looking at kernel compile queue on nodes hosting canary: queue length spiked to 12 concurrently compiled kernels, GPU memory pressure up ~18%. Logs show repeated OOM-retry on a node (node-3).

maria-ong: customer impact? any request errors or just latency?

product-oncall: we have two customers reporting slow streaming responses: session timeouts ~10s, but no 5xx errors reported yet. They flagged degraded UX.

kevin: assign mitigation steps: 1) reduce canary traffic to 5% 2) pin traffic to stable variant 3) rollback variant if necessary. What's fastest?

maria-ong: I can shift traffic. Initiating soft-traffic-stepdown to 5% now. Command: `rbctl traffic shift --model redwood-hotstart-v2 --percent 5 --grace 30s`

deploy-bot: `rbctl` acknowledged — shifting traffic to 5% over 30s.

sre-bot: Observability: p99 dropped from 2.6s -> 1.1s within 90s of traffic stepdown. Streaming stall rate decreased by ~75%.

samira: good signal that variant is the trigger. Still want to avoid user-visible impact — recommend rollback to redwood-hotstart-v1 for canary pool while we dig deeper.

ashwin: confirm rollback command and risk: rollback will trigger replacement allocations and some cold starts but should avoid the heavy kernel compile storm since v1 precompiled kernels exist.

maria-ong: initiating rollback. Command: `deployctl rollback --service inference-canary --to-tag redwood-hotstart-v1 --confirm`

deploy-bot: rollback in progress. Notifying autoscaler to prefer nodes with precompiled kernels.

kevin: notify support and affected customers that mitigation is in progress. Samira, can you circle back after rollback completes to capture root cause?

samira: yup. I'll pull kernel compile logs, NVCC traces and quantization flags used by v2. Also check if packaging added a new operator requiring separate compilation.

product-oncall: escalating to account teams for the two customers with timeouts. message template: "We've reduced canary traffic and rolled back the canary variant to restore streaming performance. We're investigating root cause and will follow up."

maria-ong: rollback finished at 11:07:10. Current canary traffic stable at 5% on v1. p99 now 0.95s. Streaming stalls at baseline.

sre-bot: Incident timeline: 
- 11:02:14 rollout v2 -> 40%
- 11:03:20 p99 spike detected
- 11:05:00 traffic stepped to 5%
- 11:07:10 rollback to v1 complete

ashwin: grabbing artifacts: kernel-compile.log (node-3), nvprof traces, and the deployed package hash for v2. I'll upload to /incidents/2178000000/artifacts.

samira: early triage: v2 ships with a new fused attention kernel requiring JIT compile on first use. We saw compile retries and fallback codepaths causing long waits. Also packaging changed the quantization backend which increased memory footprints causing fragmentation.

kevin: next actions: 1) block v2 until pre-compile pipeline is integrated 2) add rollout guard to limit concurrent kernel compiles per node 3) add automated rollback on p99 >1.5s for >3mins during rollouts.

maria-ong: creating ticket INF-7234 for rollout guards and INF-7235 for precompile pipeline. Linking artifacts.

product-oncall: customers notified, CS follow-ups scheduled.

maria-ong: final notes: if anyone needs to re-run repro in staging, use `staging-deploy --model redwood-hotstart-v2 --precompile=true` to reproduce compile sequence without impacting prod.

ashwin: thanks all. I'll continue root cause with Samira and update in this thread.

kevin: nice work — quick mitigation and clean rollback. Marking as resolved for the live incident; we will keep this thread open for RCA updates. :thumbsup:
